learningObjective: Understand XLA's Buffer Assignment: value-to-buffer mapping, liveness-based sharing, in-place execution.

canonicalClaims.claim: XLA's Buffer Assignment is a compile-time pass that assigns HLO values to physical buffers, uses liveness analysis to let disjoint-lifetime values share buffers, and enables in-place execution when analysis proves the input value is no longer needed after the op.
conditions: Static HLO program with tractable liveness analysis.
nonImplications: Does not imply zero-copy is always achievable.
Does not imply runtime allocation vanishes; dynamic allocations still exist.

misconceptions.whyWrong: It is a compile-time pass; the assignment is baked into the compiled artifact.

misconceptions.claim: Each HLO value gets its own dedicated buffer for the program lifetime.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Buffer sharing between disjoint-liveness values is a primary optimization.
In-place execution is enabled when static analysis permits.

misconceptions.claim: Buffer sharing is unsafe because of concurrent execution.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Sharing is only allowed when liveness ranges are disjoint.

implementationFacts: Buffer donation: caller can donate input buffers for in-place reuse via program parameters.
In-place ops include dynamic_update_slice under favorable liveness.
